sections.title: Strategies for Impact: Mapping Stakeholders & Issues, Modeling Impacts & Value, & Mobilizing Support
sections.description: Business and investment strategies succeed or fail not only because of markets and technologies, but also because of political institutions and the reactions of governments, investors, employees, communities, customers, activists, and other stakeholders. This course teaches an integrated strategic process for navigating these forces. Students learn to map stakeholder power and relationships, together with stakeholders’ preferences, salience, and willingness to mobilize across competing issues; model how environmental, social, political, and geopolitical developments affect impact and financial value across projects, firms, and investment portfolios; and mobilize support by adapting strategy, building coalitions, aligning internal decision-makers, strengthening trust, and  communicating credibly. Through cases, applied projects, financial models, workshops, and a competitive crisis-management simulation, students develop tools relevant to corporate strategy, consulting, public and private investing, sustainability, public policy, and civil society. The course also examines how firms and investors can align financial returns with the creation rather than depletion of natural, social, and human capital.
